hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with a smaller version: is every square a rectangle? A rectangle needs four right angles; a square has them, so yes. Use that same "does it meet the rules?" test on each choice below.
For each statement, try to invent ONE shape that breaks it. If you can, the statement is not always true.
A rhombus is a quadrilateral with four equal sides. Does a square have four equal sides?
Yes — a square has four equal sides, so every square is a rhombus. Statement B is always true.

explanation: A rhombus is defined as a quadrilateral with four equal sides. A square has four equal sides, so every square qualifies — B is always true.
Statement A breaks with a $3$-by-$8$ rectangle: four right angles, but the sides are not all equal, so it is not a square.
Statement C breaks with a slanted parallelogram, which has no right angles at all.
Statement D breaks because a trapezoid has only one pair of parallel sides, while a parallelogram needs two.

alternativeExplanations.title: Squares are the overachievers
steps: A square has four right angles (rectangle rule) and four equal sides (rhombus rule).
Meeting extra rules means a square belongs to several families at once — rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, quadrilateral.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The most-chosen wrong answer is A, "every rectangle is a square," because squares and rectangles feel like the same thing.
The direction matters: the shape with MORE rules (square) lives inside the group with fewer rules (rectangle), never the other way around.
Escape it by testing with a real object — a door is a rectangle but definitely not a square, which kills statement A instantly.
